title: Kernel selection v2: emit per-request telemetry events with sampling + PII-safe fields
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: Runtime: Added optional kernel-selection decision telemetry (sampled) to support rollout monitoring and tail-latency triage. No request content is logged; events are gated and cardinality-limited.
description:
Summary: This PR adds telemetry for kernel auto-selection v2 decisions so we can debug mis-selections, quantify selection distribution shifts during canary, and correlate tail latency with selector features. Telemetry is PII-safe (no prompts, no tool args, no user identifiers), cardinality-limited, and behind config gates with sampling.

Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 introduces SKU- and seq-regime-aware decision logic. During rollout we need (1) per-request explainability (why a kernel was chosen / why we fell back), (2) low-overhead sampling controls to avoid cost regressions, and (3) stable field semantics for replay/determinism investigations. This implements the telemetry portion of ENG-4824 and unblocks dashboards in observability-pack.

What’s included: (1) New structured event `runtime.kernel_selection.decision` emitted after selector evaluation, before kernel launch; (2) Sampling + gating: off by default, with environment/model/GPU overrides; (3) PII/capability constraints: explicit allowlist of fields, no request payload; (4) Cardinality controls: candidate kernels are emitted as a bounded list + a stable signature; (5) Light unit/integration tests validating redaction, truncation, and event determinism.

Event schema (stable fields): selector_version=v2; decision_id (uuidv4); timestamp; model_id (internal canonical id); model_family (llama/mistral/qwen/gemma/unknown); model_revision (serving rev string); gpu_sku (normalized, e.g. H100-SXM, A100-80GB, L40S; no device UUIDs); cuda_version + driver_version (coarse buckets); seq_bucket (short/medium/long/xlong); prefill_tokens_bucket + decode_tokens_bucket (bucketed, not exact); observed_regime_hint (from scheduler if present); chosen_kernel (string id); candidate_kernels (bounded list, max 6); candidate_set_sig (stable hash over sorted candidate ids); fallback_reason (enum: none|missing_kernel|denylisted|unstable_driver_guardrail|compile_cache_miss|perf_guardrail|unknown); denylist_rule_id (string, optional); gate_state (enabled/disabled + source); selection_time_us (integer); compile_cache_hit (bool); selector_cache_hit (bool); error (optional enum if selector encountered recoverable error).

Sampling and overhead: Default sampling is 0.1% (`kernel_selection.telemetry.sample_rate=0.001`) with an additional “burst” mode for canaries (up to 2% for specific {model_id,gpu_sku,region} tuples). Sampling decisions are made once per request, early, and reused across all telemetry writes for that request. Emission uses the existing async telemetry queue; at 2% on our perf-canary profiles the added CPU overhead was within noise (< ~3µs p95 in microbench; see selector perf counter logs in test output).

PII / privacy considerations: No prompt text, completions, user ids, IPs, headers, or tool payloads are recorded. The only request-linked identifier is `decision_id` and a short-lived `request_trace_id` that is already present in tracing and is not customer-provided. GPU identity uses normalized SKU only; removed raw PCIe device ids and GPU UUIDs. Token counts are bucketed to avoid leaking precise lengths for unusually structured workloads.

Operational notes: New config keys under `runtime.kernel_selection.telemetry.*` with hot-reload support. SRE can temporarily increase sampling for a model/GPU combo during incidents. This PR does not add new dashboards; it provides the underlying events/metrics that dashboard panels will query.

Testing: Added unit tests for redaction/truncation and a deterministic snapshot test for schema stability. Ran `runtime_e2e_gpu_smoke` on A100 and H100 lanes (hosted canary). CI includes lint + schema validation.

Follow-ups: Observability-pack PR will add dashboard panels keyed on `chosen_kernel`, `seq_bucket`, `gpu_sku`, and `fallback_reason`. We may also add a rate limiter on telemetry queue in a separate PR if we see backpressure at higher sampling in Dedicated pools.
commits: runtime/telemetry: add kernel selection decision event + schema
runtime/kernel_selection: plumb selector features into telemetry payload
runtime/config: add kernel_selection.telemetry sampling + gate options (hot reload)
runtime/tests: add redaction + truncation tests; schema snapshot test
docs: add internal note on PII-safe selection telemetry and field meanings
conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Please ensure we never emit raw device identifiers. I see `gpu_uuid` in the initial draft payload—this is a hard no for both privacy and cardinality. Also: bucket token counts; exact prefill length can be sensitive for some enterprise workloads.

Logan Wright (author): Ack. Removed gpu_uuid + device_id entirely; switched to `gpu_sku_norm` only. Token counts are now bucketed (powers-of-two buckets up to 32k, then 64k). Added tests that fail if any raw ids are present in payload.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics/event naming: we should keep event fields stable and versioned. Can we add `selector_version` and avoid changing field names between v1/v2? Also please cap candidate list length; otherwise dashboards will explode.

Logan Wright (author): Added `selector_version` (v1/v2) and kept field names generic (`chosen_kernel`, `candidate_kernels`). Candidate list now capped at 6 with an additional `candidate_set_sig` hash for complete set correlation. Added schema snapshot test to catch accidental field changes.

Caleb Johnson (review): Telemetry ingestion will choke if candidate_kernels is unbounded or high-cardinality strings. Can you confirm kernel ids are from a finite registry and not include build paths? Also I’d prefer truncating any unexpected string fields at source.

Logan Wright (author): Kernel ids are registry keys (e.g. `flashattn_v3_fp16`, `xformers_mha_int8`), not paths. Added a `sanitize_string()` helper with a max length (64) applied to all string fields including rule ids/fallback reasons; unknown values are coerced to `unknown`.

Jordan Lee (review): Determinism: sampling should not affect selection outcomes. Please confirm the sampling decision is computed after selector evaluation or at least not used by selector inputs. Also, do we log any non-deterministic ordering (candidate list)?

Logan Wright (author): Sampling is computed independently and only gates telemetry emission; selector inputs untouched. Candidate list is emitted in deterministic order (stable sort by kernel id) and we log a hash over the sorted set. Added a test asserting ordering determinism.
Yuki Sato (review): Nice. One more: add `fallback_reason` enum and include denylist rule id when applicable. This will help when we disable kernels per SKU/driver.
Logan Wright (author): Done. Added `fallback_reason` enum and optional `denylist_rule_id` (string). Also added `unstable_driver_guardrail` as a specific reason.
Logan Wright (author): Fixed formatting + reran lint.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. Thanks for removing gpu_uuid and bucketing token counts. This should be safe to enable at low sample rates during canary.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved with the schema snapshot test + candidate cap.
Caleb Johnson (approval): Approved. Sanitization + bounded fields look good.
Merge (squash): Merged by Logan Wright into main. Squash commit message: 'Kernel selection v2: emit per-request telemetry events with sampling + PII-safe fields' (ENG-4824).
